findings.text: POSITIONAL_ONLY parameters with defaults always appear in repr even when matching default, because the POSITIONAL_ONLY branch (line 104-105) yields just the value without checking param.default. Failing input: a class with def __init__(self, x, /, y=5) instantiated as Foo(10) will include y=5 in repr.

auto_rich_repr assumes __init__ parameter names match instance attribute names. If __init__ stores params differently (e.g., def __init__(self, v): self._v = v), getattr(self, 'v') raises AttributeError. While caught, this makes auto-generation fail for valid class designs where parameter and attribute names differ.
Dead code 'angular = angular' at line 129 is a no-op that suggests incomplete refactoring; while not causing wrong behavior, it indicates potential confusion in the decorator call pattern logic.
